title: Introduce layered build cache and slim runtime images to cut CI latency and cost
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: Our GitHub Actions pipelines and internal build clusters exhibit long cold-starts, large image layers, and suboptimal cache hit rates leading to inflated CI minutes and developer cycle time. Multiple services still build full images from heavy OS base layers and run redundant tool installs in each job. Goals: reduce median job time for the core build matrix by >=30%, cut monthly CI bill for Linux builds by >=25%, and provide a repeatable path for teams to adopt remote cache exports and lighter runtime images without service regressions.
background: We currently have heterogeneous Dockerfiles across services: variation in base images (ubuntu:18.04, Debian slim, custom u-18 snapshots), duplicated build tooling installs, and missing cache/export configuration for buildkit. Recent experiments on infra/foo service with a cache-to-registry exporter showed 3x faster rebuilds after the first push. Several lint/toolchain-related jobs still use older tool versions (golangci-lint v1.50, go1.19), causing sporadic false positives and slowing the lint stage. This ticket consolidates those learnings into a cross-repo modernization plan.
acceptance_criteria: Centralize two canonical base images (builder: debian-slim-based with build deps; runtime: distroless or deb-slim-minimal) and publish them in our private registry with automated nightly rebuilds
Enable remote build cache exports for all main Linux build jobs with cache hit telemetry in Buildkite/GHA (target hit >=70% for incremental builds)
Reduce median time of the primary build+test job across services by >=30% versus baseline snapshot (2026-02-01)
Upgrade Go toolchain for services in the migration wave to go1.20 and golangci-lint v1.56 (or newer) with an automated compatibility test job
Document migration guide and provide a small CLI script to opt-in service Dockerfiles to layered builds and cache exporters
No production image size regressions (>5%) after switching to slim/distroless runtime images and passing smoke tests
tasks: Audit top-30 fastest-changing repos to collect Dockerfile variants and list duplicated install steps (owner: Miguel)
Create two canonical Dockerfiles: Dockerfile.canonical.builder and Dockerfile.canonical.runtime, publish to registry with tags 'redwood/builder:stable' and 'redwood/runtime:stable' (owner: Evan)
Add BuildKit config and 'cache-to=registry' exporters to GHA/Buildkite workflows; enable cache pruning policy (owner: Priya)
Prototype multi-stage layer splitting for python wheel build vs runtime surface to reduce layer churn (owner: SRE team)
Roll out a golangci-lint config standard and add 'lint-stable' job that runs in parallel to the main PR check (owner: DevEx)
Implement telemetry dashboards: cache hit ratio, average image size, job median duration, and CI cost by repo (owner: Observability)
Ship migration PR templates and a migration checklist for service owners; provide 1:1 office hours for first cohort (owner: Miguel)
Run canary rollout on 5 non-critical services and validate cache hit rates and runtime smoke tests before broad rollout (owner: Release)
Add rollback instructions and emergency switch to previous image tags in case of failures (owner: Miguel)
Post-migration retrospective and lessons learned doc (owner: Asha)
Follow-up: evaluate pnpm workspace / shared node cache for frontend repos if time permits (stretch goal)
